attacks.claim: The embargo badge text is hard-coded to #ffffff on a background of var(--surface), which is also #ffffff in the default light theme. The label is effectively invisible for default-theme editors, failing WCAG 1.4.3 and hiding the embargo information.

The unpublish control is a span with only an onClick handler. It is not focusable, has no button role or keyboard activation, has no accessible name (the icon is aria-hidden), and has no :focus-visible style. Keyboard-only and screen-reader editors cannot find, identify, or operate it, failing WCAG 2.1.1, 2.4.7, and 4.1.2 for a release-required path.
attacks.evidence: ; .unpublish:hover only; ABSENT: focus style, aria-label, or a native button

attacks.claim: handleUnpublish has no try/catch and no pending state. A rejected onUnpublish is unhandled and gives the editor no feedback, and repeated activation while a request is in flight can trigger duplicate unpublish calls.
attacks.evidence: if (ok) await onUnpublish(draft.id); with no error handling or busy state

attacks.claim: Once the trigger is made focusable, nothing in the diff returns focus to it after the confirm dialog closes, so keyboard users lose their place in the queue.
attacks.evidence: const ok = await confirm({ ... }); ABSENT: focus return to the trigger

attacks.claim: The embargo lift time is shown without a timezone label even though it is expressed in the newsroom timezone. Editors in other zones may read it as local time.

The embargoed determination uses the client clock (new Date()), so badge visibility can be wrong with a skewed clock. This is a display issue only, since the diff does not change any publish gate, but it should be confirmed that the server enforces embargo.
attacks.evidence: const embargoed = draft.embargoUntil !== null && new Date(draft.embargoUntil) > new Date();

attacks.claim: The unpublish action is shown for every published draft with no permission check in the diff. Server-side authorization for unpublish should be confirmed, since queue access may be broader than the roles allowed to pull stories.
attacks.evidence: {draft.status === "published" && (<span className={styles.unpublish} onClick={handleUnpublish}>; ABSENT: role or permission gate in the diff

attacks.claim: The PR has no feature flag or documented rollback for the new embargo badge and unpublish control, so they cannot be disabled quickly in production if they misbehave.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: feature flag or revert plan in the PR body; change ships in DraftRow.tsx and the shared tokens.css
